entries.title: Margin notes can explain, remind and flag tensions
entries.body: The notes in the margin beside your article can include a few short ones of their own: an explanation, a reminder of an earlier passage, a tension between two passages, or an aside, each stamped Note, Recall or Tension. Every quote a note uses is checked against the passage it names, and one that does not match is dropped. Articles you added before get the new notes when you next show the margin with the window wide enough for it.

entries.title: Explore in Learn is open to everyone
entries.body: Explore, beside Tutorial in Learn, no longer needs the Experimental features switch on your profile page. It is where you take your own line of thought about the article further, and Tutorial points you there when you start one.

entries.title: Cited by works for pieces without a DOI
entries.body: The Cited by list used to need a DOI, the identifier a published paper carries. For a web page or blog post without one, it can search the OpenAlex research catalogue by title and author, accepts only a single close match, and links that record so you can check it. The privacy policy says titles may go to OpenAlex.

entries.title: A gifted article can become yours
entries.body: When you sign in to claim a gift that came with an article, the article can move into your library with everything already built for it, made private; the link it came on stops working. The giver's notes and settings are removed, not passed on. If it cannot move, your gift is still claimed and the article stays put.

entries.title: The guide suggests, and you press the button
entries.body: The guide no longer opens a mode or moves you through the article by itself after it answers; everything it suggests is a button for you to press. The box you type into is easier to spot, with larger text and its own background, and it starts at two lines and grows as you write. Suggestions sit centred beneath it.

entries.title: Search and add are easier to tell apart
entries.body: At the top of your library, the search box sits on the right and says "Search your shelf", and the box for adding an article sits on the left and asks for a link. Paste a link into search and it offers to add that article; type words into the add box and it points you to search.
